body.name: Mixed-support atlas handle
body.construction:
On input \(T\), construct \(\mathscr A\) by enumerating the labeled rank and support data in \(\Sigma(T)\): use oriented segment boxes on rank-two cells, the disjoint \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm E,\mathrm D\) modes on rank-one cells, coordinatewise bounded splits on equal-endpoint cells, shared endpoint variables, and the residual-ratio forest on design-B charts.  Denote the resulting one-copy semialgebraic charts by \(X_\chi\); their design-specific unions are \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) and \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).  Test every chart for emptiness.  If all are empty, report incompatibility.  Otherwise sample one \(x_0\in\bigcup_\chi X_\chi\), set \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\), and for each \(\chi\) test the one-copy refinement
\[
 X_\chi\cap\left\{x:
 \bigl(\tau_{C,1}(x)-t_{0,1}\bigr)^2+
 \bigl(\tau_{C,2}(x)-t_{0,2}\bigr)^2>0\right\}.
\]
If every refinement is empty, return \(t_0\); if one is nonempty, sample it and lift the resulting pair into \(\mathcal F_A\) or \(\mathcal F_B\).  Work over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) and its ordered finite extension generated by \(t_0\).  Connected-component descriptions and target projections are optional diagnostics, not decision stages.
